content:
- Model consistently overestimates prices, especially in the early part of the forecast horizon (first 5–10 days).
- Forecasts tend to peak too early and overshoot true values after sharp spikes in history.
- Model exhibits mean reversion bias: overestimates after recent high prices, underestimates after recent lows.
- Forecasts lag behind true values by 1–3 days in the middle to late horizon (days 15–30).
- Model fails to capture sustained upward trends in the 30-day window; underestimates when true values rise steadily.
- Overconfidence in short-term momentum leads to overestimation of volatility in early days.
- Model underestimates true values when history shows strong upward momentum (e.g., 75–78 range → forecast 76–77).
- Forecasts are overly smooth; fail to reflect sharp, sudden price reversals or corrections.
- Model tends to underestimate true values in the final 5–10 days of the forecast horizon, especially when true values are trending down.
